subject: Issue modeling finite mixtures when using user-defined non-Euclidean detection function

messages.author: 3451c2e31f1fe160
messages.subject: Issue modeling finite mixtures when using user-defined non-Euclidean detection function
parts:
Hello Murray et al.,

I have a Peromyscus sp. capture-recapture dataset comprised of 33 individuals that were detected 80 times over 5 occasions. The sampling occurred on 3 grids of 100 traps each, located along the bottom of a linearly oriented northwest to southeast canyon (azimuth of approximately 105 degrees). Thus, I have reason to believe that the base assumption of Euclidean detection/movement (i.e., bivariate normal or isotropic) is not appropriate for this system. 

Indeed, I used the user-defined non-Euclidean (anisotropic) detection function that we previously developed (see Murphy et al. 2016. J. Wild. Mgmt. 80:1390-1407) in a null model (D~1, g0~1, sigma~1) and compared that to the same null model with an isotropic detection function; the anisotropic model had an AICc value that was 10 units lower than the isotropic model. Clearly, the anisotropic detection functions should be used. As an aside, habitat and elevation where the grids were located were relatively homogeneous, so using Royle's LCP ecological distance won't work.

Nonetheless, I need to consider sex-specific detection and movement to account for potential heterogeneity. However, when I model the 2-class finite mixtures (h2) on g0 or sigma, with hcov = "Sex", in combination with my anisotropic detection function, the models do not run. Below is the error that I keep getting from R:

> mod1a=secr.fit (alldata, hcov = "Sex", model=list(D~1, g0~h2, sigma~1), mask = maskCovs,details=list(userdist=mydistfn),
+                link = list(noneuc = 'log'), start = list(noneuc =exp(-0.4)))
Checking data 
Preparing detection design matrices 
Preparing density design matrix 
Preparing non-Euclidean parameter design matrix 
Finding initial parameter values... 
Initial values  D = 3.34721, g0 = 0.01704, sigma = 47.10141 
Maximizing likelihood... 
Eval     Loglik        D       g0   g0.h2M    sigma pmix.h2M   noneuc 
Error in (function (f, p, ..., hessian = FALSE, typsize = rep(1, length(p)),  : 
  missing value in parameter

I initially thought that this was either an issue with the starting value or with maximization, so I tried numerous different starting values ranging from exp(-4) to exp (4), but continuously received the same error. I then used the OVpossum example provided in the non-Euclidean vignette and added h2 to g0; the same error was received:

datadir <-  system.file(  "extdata"  ,  package =    "secr")
ovforest <- rgdal::  readOGR(  dsn =    paste0  (datadir,    "/OVforest.shp"  ),  layer =    "OVforest")
eftbank <-  read.table(  paste0 (datadir,    "/leftbank.txt"  ))[    21    :      195    ,]# for plotting
ovposs <- OVpossumCH[[  1  ]]# February 1996
ovmask <-  make.mask(  traps  (ovposs),  buffer =    120  ,  type =    "trapbuffer"  ,  poly =    ovforest[1: 2 ,],  spacing =    7.5  ,  keep.poly =    FALSE)

fn1 <- function (xy1, xy2, mask) {
  if (    missing    (xy1))    return  (    "noneuc"  ) 
  sig <-    covariates  (mask)$noneuc  # sigma(x,y) at mask points
  sig <-    matrix  (sig,    byrow =      TRUE    ,    nrow =      nrow    (xy1),    ncol =      nrow    (xy2)) 
  euc <-    edist  (xy1, xy2) 
  euc / sig
  }
fit1 <-  secr.fit(ovposs,  model=list(D~1, g0~h2, sigma~1,noneuc ~ x + y + x2 + y2 + xy),mask = ovmask ,  trace = FALSE  ,  details =  list(userdist = fn1),  fixed =list(sigma =1  ))


Thus, there appears to be a bug in secr (v3.0.1) that prevents non-Euclidean detection functions from being used with h2 mixtures. Has anyone had a similar issue or know of a way to resolve this issue?


Thanks,

Sean

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Issue modeling finite mixtures when using user-defined non-Euclidean detection function
parts:
Hi Sean
Yes, there seems to be a bug when mixtures are used with noneuc. I think the code used to assume that pmix was the last parameter, which doesn't work with noneuc also appearing. This may take me a few days to fix. Thanks for the report. I would like to discuss whether you really need noneuc, and the risks of aligning your trap lines with the supposed direction of elongation of home ranges, but first I should deal with the bug!
Murray

messages.subject: Re: Issue modeling finite mixtures when using user-defined non-Euclidean detection function
parts:
Hey Murray,

Thanks for the quick response and for looking into this issue. I look forward to giving it a run after you work your magic!

To clarify, the sampling grids were not intentionally aligned linearly because of the possible direction of elongation of home ranges. Instead, suitable habitat for the species of interest was located at a canyon floor that is bounded to the north and south by cliffs, and the canyon is approximately linear. Thus, the exploration of home range elongation along the canyon's direction is post hoc.

Sean
